payload.name: Preserve Exhibition Context for Created Works
payload.description: When a speaker mentions a work (painting, book, etc.) that is finished, published, or exhibited, during extraction include the publication/exhibition detail in the memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker describes finishing or creating a work (e.g., painting, book, song) and also states that it is published, exhibited, or displayed, capture that contextual detail in the same event memory or as a related event/relationship memory.
Do not create a candidate that only records the creation action; preserve all explicitly stated identifiers that would let a future question identify the specific work.
During CRUD, when adding or updating memories about a created work, do not merge away an existing publication/exhibition detail unless new evidence directly contradicts it.
Stop after capturing the explicitly stated context; do not infer additional locations or publication details.

solves: When extraction summarizes an event about a created work, it can drop the contextual detail that identifies the work (e.g., that it was exhibited or published), making the memory insufficient for later questions that refer to that work by its context. This Skill ensures such explicit identifiers are preserved.
